operations.value: Parse and validate every target-specific SPI value supplied by OPEN. Construct SpiConnectionSettings using clockFrequency, mode, dataFlow, chipSelectActiveState and configuration from the request; do not embed their selected target values in generated module source. Map mode by exact tokens Mode0, Mode1, Mode2 or Mode3; map dataFlow by exact tokens MsbFirst or LsbFirst; parse chipSelectActiveState as true or false case-insensitively; map configuration by the SpiBusConfiguration names supported by the selected platform. Create the SX1262 driver and return EOPEN if the resulting driver is null; create AutoDrain RX and Manual TX queues; attach exactly three named handlers. Validate busId, cs and busy >=0; rst and irq >=-1; clockFrequency >0. Forward -1 unchanged to the existing driver; do not change driver implementation.

Disable delivery, detach named Press and Holding callbacks and dispose GpioButton with shouldDispose=false so its pin is released. Retain the SYS module controller and all subscriptions; do not close the button pin twice. Preserve last successful OPEN configuration; reset hardware/interaction state only.
Selected nanoFramework PinMode.ToString() representation; the tested firmware renders InputPullUp as 2. This patch does not introduce normalized enum-name output.
+DATA:<ctx>,SYS:button,opened=<bool>,pin=<gpio|-1>,mode=<mode>,debounceMs=<n>,holding=<bool>

Defaults apply before the first successful OPEN. Successful new OPEN atomically commits the validated binding; failed OPEN and OPEN-already preserve the last successful binding. CLOSE releases hardware but retains this binding; repeated CLOSE is idempotent. INFO is available open or closed; opened derives only from the nullable hardware object. Reopening still requires explicit OPEN arguments; no new implicit OPEN form.
